issues.evidence: results-canonical-regressions.json: prior release reports zero widget/text/raster changes in both controlled public cases; current code reports one document-level field change. pypdf independently confirms saved values, export/display mapping and absence of widgets in the unplaced case.
issues.limits: Document-level records coexist with widget records; counts are not additive. Changed-source interactive documents still require review.

issues.evidence: results-form-user-unit.json: all 14 public form inventories match pypdf, including eight XFA hybrids; 47 supported declared values checked. results-hybrid-regressions.json reproduces the prior missed AcroForm value change and verifies one current document-level change with unchanged painting and no placed widgets.
issues.limits: XFA XML semantics remain unverified and produce a separate review diagnostic. This is AcroForm inventory/value coverage, not proof of full form behavior.

issues.evidence: Native and shared Chrome/WASM fixtures preserve known changes despite an unreadable V, compare literal and compressed text/JavaScript streams, and reject corrupt/truncated/trailing or overexpanded encodings. Each unreadable property is retained in unavailable_properties and counted in comparison.canonical_properties_unavailable.
issues.limits: Only identity, FlateDecode and ASCIIHexDecode text/JavaScript streams with supported dictionary keys and no-op parameters are decoded. Unsupported property values remain unknown, not absent. Tree/identity errors still disable the source snapshot to avoid false additions/removals; exhausted work budgets fail the complete snapshot.

issues.evidence: Unreferenced orphan fields, signature verification, full action semantics, rich-text/default-appearance/resource normalization and AcroForm-level flags/calculation order are not fully modeled. Raw binary signature values are not signature verification.
issues.required: Extend independently checked coverage without marking changed-source interactive documents complete prematurely.

issues.evidence: lopdf 0.46.0 limits individual object/xref stream expansion to 8MiB, and the application limits source size, traversal depth/items and output work. These do not bound every internal parser allocation or total elapsed time. Text/action decoding strictly validates complete streams, reserves bounded output work before decompression, and charges failed reservations. Eager internal object/xref parsing still relies on lopdf and is outside this strict text-stream decoder.
issues.required: Add aggregate/process memory and time isolation for untrusted parsing/decoding; retain recoverable diagnostics and native/WASM parity.

implementation_profile.text_output_budget: min(max_input_mb MiB,64MiB), conservative charge for JSON escaping and repeated qualified name components
implementation_profile.normalization: Strict BOM-marked UTF-16BE and UTF-8; one-byte PDFDocEncoding rejects undefined scalars. Dictionary and field order normalized; reference identities resolved. Stored values retain literal Unicode/array order.
implementation_profile.text_stream_integrity: Complete stream, checksum, end marker and trailing-data checks. At most 16 filters, 8MiB per decoded layer, and aggregate reserved work including failed attempts. Unsupported filter/parameter/dictionary semantics remain unavailable.

current_qualification: results-user-unit.json reexecutes all three public canonical mutations, including the hybrid case, with the current binary. Historical before/after reports remain under their original hashes.
